title: Intermodal combined PET/MRI examination to measure the activity of the mesolimbic brain system after stress exposure
summary: The brain's reward system plays a central role in the development and maintenance of alcohol dependence. Studies have been shown that changes in the activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine and in the brain's response to alcohol-related stimuli (cue reactivity) are associated with increased alcohol cravings and increased risk of relapse. Psychosocial stress can additionally influence these processes by increasing alcohol craving and dopamine activity in the reward system. In this study, we investigate the effects of stress on dopamine activity and the neural activity to alcohol stimuli in test subjects with an alcohol use disorder for the first time using a combined PET/MRI examination. The aim is to gain a better understanding of the neurobiological mechanisms involved in the development of alcohol craving and to uncover possible links with the risk of relapse.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of alcohol dependence according to ICD 10 or alcohol use disorder according to DSM-5 and score on the Alcohol Dependence Scale (ADS) < 31 points (i.e. below the range of "very severe dependence")
- Abstinence before initial examination of 7 days
- Sufficient ability to communicate with the respective study staff, answer questions and complete questionnaires
- Written consent available
Exclusion criteria:
- Contraindication for a PET or MRI scan
- Presence of withdrawal symptoms (CIWA score > 3) at the time of the examination
- Breath alcohol > 0.0 per mille at the time of the examination and/or lack of abstinence between the two days of the examination
- Presence of an Axis I disorder (DSM-5), except nicotine use disorder, anxiety disorder, remitted affective disorder and mild to moderate depressive episode
- Current use of psychotropic medication
- Glucocorticoid metabolism disorders, use of glucocorticoid-containing medications or medications that interact with glucocorticoids
- For female participants: Pregnancy or planned pregnancy
- Participation in a study with ionising radiation within the last 5 years
- Presence of acute suicidal behaviour or acute danger to self or others
- Current use of illegal substances, opiates or sedatives
